plain_description.what: Checks whether the two certified splits of the main tree (Chemistry and Engineering) stay certified when the tree is rebuilt on two other random train/test draws. Also checks a stricter top-down multiple-testing rule. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: A certificate that disappears when the data are redrawn would be fragile. This measures how stable the tree's two showcase splits are.
plain_description.information: Surviving both redraws would make the splits robust; surviving one would make them draw-dependent. Result (descriptive, and the analysts had already seen the data): each split is certified on the main tree and on 1 of the 2 redraws. On the other redraw nothing is certified. Under the stricter rule, Chemistry passes on two of the three trees, and Engineering cannot pass at all with 300 repetitions. The redraws are only id-disjoint, not content-disjoint.
